A fetal anatomic survey on follow-up antepartum sonograms may be clinically useful in identifying unanticipated fetal anomalies, especially when the indication is for fetal growth. This type of assessment can help healthcare providers detect potential issues early on, allowing them to take prompt action to ensure the best possible outcomes for both the mother and the baby.

While it's essential to note that not all sonograms will show abnormalities, a thorough examination can help identify potential problems that may be causing concerns or anomalies. This is particularly important when considering fetal growth, as any issues may impact future health outcomes.
